title: Granular event retention, reindexing and backfill checklist
content:
Purpose:
This note is a compact operational cheat-sheet describing the desired event/audit retention tiers, TTL rules, index layout, and safe backfill/reindex procedures we should use for Redwood Inference audit events and SIEM exports. It focuses on implementation details, failure modes, and recovery steps that are operationally actionable (for SREs, infra, and security engineers).

Scope:
- Applies to all system-generated audit events (authn/authz, API requests, admin console actions, model deployments) and evidence artifacts derived from these events.
- Excludes ephemeral debug traces and purely application telemetry (handled by observability pipelines).
- Includes export to downstream SIEMs (forwards), object store retention (evidence blobs), and nearline indexed store used by Console and forensic queries.

Design principles (short):
- Keep hot index small and query-fast: 30–90 day hot window depending on event class.
- Make backfills resumable and idempotent. Track checkpoints per partition.
- Prefer append-only immutable blobs + logical tombstones for DSR/retention deletions to preserve auditability of deletion workflows.
- Minimize reindexing by using well-planned index templates and time-based partitions.
- Ensure RBAC v2 metadata is attached to index documents so access controls are auditable.

Retention buckets (recommended):
- Hot (0–30 days default for high-volume auth/API events): full document, indexed, fast shards, replicated.
- Warm (31–90 days): indexed but fewer replicas and slower hardware; shards can be merged/compacted.
- Cold (91–365 days): compressed indexes or return to object store with smaller search capability; query paths go through rehydration or precomputed aggregates.
- Frozen / Archive (365+): compressed object-store blobs (S3 Glacier Deep Archive or equivalent). Indexed pointers retained if allowed by policy. Evidence blobs kept for minimum compliance window (configurable per customer).

Event class TTL guidance (examples):
- AuthN/AuthZ (successful & failed logins): Hot 90d, Warm 275d, Cold 1y, Archive 7y (per enterprise contract).
- Admin console actions (deploy/rollout changes): Hot 180d, Cold 2y, Archive 7y.
- API request/response traces (high volume): Hot 30d, Warm 60d, Cold 6mo. Store only a sampling of full payloads beyond hot window.
- Evidence blobs (customer files): retention per contract + legal holds; keep encrypted object + manifest in index until deletion request processed.

Storage mapping (example implementation):
- Hot/Warm/Cold indexes: Managed Elasticsearch/OpenSearch clusters with ILM policies; time-based indices named events-YYYY.MM (or weekly for high volume).
- Archive: S3 bucket with path: s3://redwood-evidence/<customer>/<year>/events-<date>.ndjson.gzip; manifest file contains index_id, min_ts, max_ts, checksum, reingest-hints.
- SIEM export: Kafka topic per environment and SIEM destination; delivery guarantees at-least-once with consumer checkpoints.

Indexing strategy and schema notes:
- Time-partitioned indices to limit reindex surface: indices by month or week depending on ingestion volume.
- Index templates set mapping: explicit types for user_id, actor_type, resource_id, action, outcome, region, cluster_id, tags, rbactags. Avoid dynamic mapping where possible.
- Store a compact canonical JSON in _source; also store a small denormalized header for common search fields (actor, action, outcome, ts, tenant_id, rbactags).
- Document ID scheme: sha256(timestamp + tenant_id + trace_id + event_type) to avoid duplicates across reingests.
- Add metadata fields for provenance: ingest_pipeline_version, original_ingest_time, object_store_path (if blob exists).

Backfill and reindex choreography (pattern):
1) Plan: define source time ranges, target index template, throughput targets, and estimated cost. Create a backfill ticket with owners and runbook.
2) Snapshot source: export event set to ndjson.gz in object-store with manifest (partitioned by hour/day). Include event checksums.
3) Dry run small sample through the ingestion pipeline to verify mapping and pipeline transforms.
4) Compute mapping diffs and if necessary create new index template and new time-partitioned target indices.
5) Use an orchestrator (Airflow / Temporal) to run parallel workers that: read manifest partition -> transform -> write to target with idempotent upsert semantics (create_if_not_exists).
6) Checkpoint: workers update a centralized checkpoint store (DynamoDB / Spanner / Postgres) per partition and per worker to support resume. Checkpoints store last_processed_offset, checksum, worker_id.
7) Consistency verification step after each partition: checksum of target documents vs source manifest.
8) On success, update routing/alias to include new indices. Keep old indices for 7–14 days for rollback.

Idempotency and deduplication rules:
- Use deterministic doc IDs and upsert semantics so repeated replays don’t create duplicates.
- When schema changes are unavoidable, reindex into new index name, and create alias swap after verification.
- For object-blobs, compare checksum before re-upload to avoid extraneous copies.

Failure modes and recovery (common):
- Worker crash mid-partition: resume using partition checkpoint; idempotent write prevents duplication.
- Mapping mismatch: small sample dry-run should catch; if missed, stop and create new target mapping. Recovery requires reindex into new index and alias swap.
- Resource exhaustion (heap/OOM): scale consumers down and increase parallelism only after heap GC/stability checks. Use backpressure (Kafka throttling) to protect ES cluster.
- Partial delivery to SIEMs (consumer errors): maintain per-message dead-letter topic and retry queue; escalate after N retries with alert.
- Archive restoration latency (rehydration too slow for console queries): precompute and cache aggregates for cold queries; add UI notice for rehydration > t.

Operational monitors and alerts (examples):
- ingestion-latency.p95 > 10s (alert page)
- index-refresh-errors.rate > 0.5% over 5m (alert page)
- backfill-checkpoint-staleness > 10m (pager if in active backfill)
- dsk_usage.index_nodes > 75% (warning), > 90% (pager)
- siem-export-failure-rate > 1% over 5m (pager)
- archive-rehydration-time.p50 > 30s (warning)
- evidence-deletion-queue-length > 0 for > 24h (pager)

Playbook: incident steps by failure class
- Backfill worker stuck / failing: 1) Check worker logs for mapping errors. 2) Verify checkpoint store. 3) Pause incoming backfill jobs, run a 1-hour sample reindex locally. 4) If mapping issue found, create new index template and re-run restartable partitions.
- SIEM export lagging: 1) Check Kafka end offsets vs consumer offsets. 2) Check SIEM endpoint health and rate-limiting headers. 3) Enable DLQ and requeue failed messages. 4) If endpoint unrecoverable, switch to buffered S3 export and notify security.
- Index corruption / shard failures: 1) Run cluster health checks. 2) Isolate failing node, allocate replicas, re-route shards. 3) Restore from snapshots if data lost. 4) Rehydrate indexes from object-store snapshots if required.

Data subject requests (DSR) and deletions:
- DSRs must be applied consistently across hot/warm/cold/archive:
  - Mark the record with tombstone in index (preserves deletion action in audit trail) and remove or redact blob in object-store following customer contract and legal hold.
  - Record the deletion action as a new audit event (who/when/how) stored for compliance as a separate reconciled log (deletion-proof record).
  - Maintain a DSR manifest per tenant listing deletions applied, retention expiry for deletion-proof records.

RBAC v2 integration notes:
- Index documents must contain rbactags array (role patterns, team ids, sensitivity labels) used by the Console and query gateway to enforce per-document access.
- Changes to RBAC policy must be recorded as an audit event and retained in hot/warm indices.
- During backfills, re-attach rbactags using historical RBAC snapshots referenced in manifest to ensure queries during reindex match original access semantics.

SIEM export mapping checklist:
- Ensure canonical fields exist: event_id, ts_iso, tenant_id, actor_type, actor_id, action, resource_type, resource_id, outcome, src_ip, user_agent, trace_id.
- Normalize enums: outcome -> {success, failure, ignored}. action -> structured action verb + subtype (deploy.rollback).
- Enrich events with geo/region and model_id where applicable before export to SIEM to reduce downstream joins.
- Export format: NDJSON gzip with header manifest + incremental sequence numbers to allow consumers to resume.

Cost guidance (quick):
- Hot index cost ~= (daily_ingest_tokens * avg_doc_size_bytes * 30 days) * ES replication factor * storage_price.
- Archive cost: object-store storage_price * retention_months + retrieval_cost estimate.
- Backfill cost estimate = IO_cost + transient compute cost * hours. Always budget 10–30% overhead for retries.

Open risks & action items:
- Need a standard manifest schema for archive exports that includes RBAC snapshot id and pipeline_version. (ACTION: owners for manifest schema: Ethan Walker, due 2025-01-10)
- Define SLA for rehydration latency visible in Console (proposal: p50 < 8s, p95 < 30s for warm->hot rehydrate). (ACTION: Security + Console product to align)
- Verify DSR deletion-proof record retention window meets legal. (ACTION: Legal + Security)

Appendix: Example sample reingest command (pseudo):
- airflow trigger_dag 'audit_backfill' --conf '{"manifest_s3":"s3://redwood-evidence/backfills/2024-09-01/manifest.json","target_index":"events-2024.09","parallelism":24}'

- sample ES upsert body (pseudo-ndjson):
{"index":{"_id":"<sha256>"}}
{"ts":"2024-09-01T12:03:10Z","tenant_id":"acct-123","actor":"svc-ingest","action":"model.deploy","outcome":"success","rbactags":["team:platform","sensitivity:low"],"ingest_pipeline_version":"v3.2","original_object_path":"s3://.../part-0001.ndjson.gz"}

If you use this runbook for an actual backfill, please add to the backfill ticket: start_ts, end_ts, manifest location, expected bytes, owner, on_call and rollback plan.

Notes (quick history):
- Drafted after incidents SIEM-EXPORT-1283 and backfill flapping in 2024 Q4. Prior fixes reduced duplicate ingestion but we still need standardized manifests and RBAC snapshot handling for forensic fidelity.

End of cheat-sheet.
